summary: CAND-2026-06-12-A91C37E5 — HarnessX reports large cross-benchmark gains from evolving typed agent harnesses, creating a useful contrast with HARNESSEVO's localized-credit result — revisit if: Independent reproduction appears, a paper-tagged release or exact benchmark/evolution manifests are published, or matched controls separate model/backbone, harness composition, adaptation compute, verifier leakage and component-level credit. CAND-2026-07-15-CHINA-ANTHROPOMORPHIC-AI-RULES — China's dedicated anthropomorphic-AI interaction rules enter force with dependency, manipulation and minor-protection duties — revisit if: CAC or other agencies publish enforcement cases, implementing standards, safety-assessment guidance, filing data or interpretations affecting agent memory/personalization/autonomy. CAND-2026-08-02-EU-AI-ACT-ENFORCEMENT — EU AI Act enters an enforcement phase for GPAI and transparency obligations — revisit if: Commission enforcement actions, GPAI guidance updates, Code-of-Practice implementation evidence, complaints/decisions or material court/regulator interpretations appear. CAND-2026-08-02-EU-GPAI-ENFORCEMENT — European Commission enforcement powers for general-purpose AI model obligations enter application — revisit if: The Commission announces a first GPAI enforcement action, systemic-risk notification decision, serious-incident proceeding, fine, or material interpretive update. CAND-2026-08-18-FDA-GENAI-MEDICAL-DEVICES — FDA opens competency-based regulatory framework discussion for generative-AI medical devices — revisit if: FDA publishes docket comments, workshop material, draft/final guidance, legal-authority analysis or concrete submission expectations before the deadline. CAND-2026-08-26-ANTHROPIC-CVD-SCALE — Anthropic's disclosure ledger shows AI-assisted vulnerability discovery scaling to thousands of human-reviewed findings — revisit if: The dashboard materially changes, per-model discovery attribution/cost is released, or independent organizations publish matched AI-versus-human vulnerability-discovery throughput. CAND-2026-08-26-AWS-NVIDIA-2M-GPU-EXPANSION — AWS and NVIDIA plan 2 million additional Blackwell Ultra/Rubin-class GPUs across 2027–2028 — revisit if: AWS discloses installed/deployed counts, Rubin instances reach GA, procurement/power buildout data appears, or timelines materially change. CAND-2026-08-31-3C91A8D4 — European Commission designates ChatGPT a Very Large Online Search Engine under the Digital Services Act — revisit if: The Commission publishes the designation decision, compliance deadline, systemic-risk requirements, audit/researcher-access details, enforcement actions or OpenAI implementation changes. CAND-2026-08-31-4F2C8E11 — EuroHPC signs €387.8M AMD MI430X LUMI-AI contract for 2027 deployment — revisit if: EuroHPC/CSC publish accelerator counts, peak/sustained AI performance, access policy or deployment milestones; installation begins; or the contract/system architecture materially changes. CAND-2026-08-31-54C150C8 — China MIIT launches national AI application-service-provider cultivation action — revisit if: MIIT publishes the national resource pool, procurement/compute-support figures, standards, adoption results, provider lists, or measurable model/agent deployment outcomes. CAND-2026-08-31-5BE9E260 — Signal: draft IPO documents reportedly show a $5.5B OpenAI warrant position in SB Energy as AI infrastructure financing deepens — revisit if: SB Energy IPO filing, SEC document, OpenAI/SoftBank/NVIDIA statement, audited financing document, or additional independent reporting confirms or contradicts the warrant and guarantee details. CAND-2026-08-31-A11F0A7E — Maniformer reports a million-hour multimodal human-interaction corpus and 20,000-device collection fleet for Physical AI — revisit if: Public dataset slices, model/data cards, independent quality audits, VLA scaling curves, privacy/consent documentation, customer training results or cross-embodiment transfer measurements appear. CAND-2026-08-31-A1C3550A — HUMAIN puts AMD MI355X/Cisco AI infrastructure into production in Saudi Arabia and targets a much larger sovereign compute buildout — revisit if: Installed accelerator count, power draw, acceptance benchmark, pricing, customer workload metrics, independent utilization data, MI400 phase commissioning, or sovereign-AI procurement documents appear. CAND-2026-08-31-AGENT-CAPABILITY-COST-EVAL — Agent capability-cost evaluation: cheaper failure is not a Pareto win, and run provenance is load-bearing — revisit if: A larger attempt-linked dataset, repeated trials, pinned model/tool configurations or independent harness comparisons appear. CAND-2026-08-31-C43E30F0 — China's Intelligent Chemical Model 3.0 Pro moves a vertical model toward tool-executing chemical-engineering workflows — revisit if: Technical report, benchmark protocol, model/data card, reproducible agent tasks, pilot-plant closed-loop results, safety/audit details or independent industrial evaluation appears. CAND-2026-08-31-CHINA-NATIONAL-AI-COMPUTE-SCALE — China reports 2.45 million PFLOPS FP16 of national intelligent-compute capacity and expanding centralized scheduling — revisit if: National Data Administration publishes methodology, accelerator inventory/utilization, energy data, task-level scheduling statistics, or independent capacity estimates suitable for cross-country comparison. CAND-2026-08-31-CN-AI-APPLICATION-SERVICE-PROVIDERS — China MIIT launches national AI application-service-provider program with explicit demand-side procurement support — revisit if: new evidence CAND-2026-08-31-CONFIDENCE-CHANNEL-DIVERGENCE — Linguistic confidence is a lossy and poorly calibrated channel for internal model confidence — revisit if: Independent reproduction, stronger black-box calibration methods, or adaptive-compute/agent-routing studies compare verbal confidence against internal or ensemble uncertainty at matched cost. CAND-2026-08-31-CXMT-HBM4-SIGNAL — Signal: CXMT reportedly begins small-scale HBM4 production — revisit if: CXMT or a named customer confirms HBM4 shipments/specifications, teardown/benchmark evidence appears, packaging partners disclose volume, or multiple independent sources corroborate yield and scale. title: Research desk digest
summary: agents_memory xAI describes Grok 4.7's longer-horizon training and reports multi-hour task results — importance 5/10 · In a September 21 release, xAI described Grok 4.7 as using a larger base than Grok 4.6, a longer reinforcement-learning run weighted toward harder multi-hour tasks, and training to understand the Grok Bot harness. The release reports Grok 4.7 scores across coding, office, terminal, legal, electrical-engineering and clinical benchmarks, including 37.6% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 versus 20.3% for Grok 4.6. These are company-reported results; the page does not provide test protocols, sample sizes or uncertainty. — FCMO-3B81F3E90D86 compute_hardware Marvell announces 2nm 400G-per-lane optical demonstrations aimed at 3.2T AI data-center links — importance 4/10 · In a September 21, 2026 announcement for ECOC, Marvell said it planned to demonstrate 2nm 400G-per-lane optical PAM4 and described it as enabling a transition toward 3.2T data-center connectivity. The company also announced planned 2nm 800G ZR/ZR+ pluggables with MACsec and 1.6T ZR/coherent-lite demonstrations. The source establishes the company’s announcement and intended showcase, not independent observation of the demos or measured product performance. It provides no lane power, optical reach, error rate, qualification status or production schedule for the 400G/lane technology. — FCMO-A4319B48FABA efficiency Constrained binary optimization selects non-consecutive transformer blocks for depth pruning — importance 5/10 · A September 11 revision of a preprint formulates transformer-block removal as a constrained binary optimization problem. It uses second-order interactions among binary keep/remove variables, derived from calibration-set gradients, to rank block combinations; several low-energy configurations may be worth testing because the lowest-energy one is not always best downstream. Without retraining, the authors report that removing 40 of 80 Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct blocks yields 76.9 MMLU for their method versus 54.0 for block influence, a 22.9-point difference, with better scores across the listed benchmarks. They also report results on a heterogeneous Nemotron MoE model without retraining. Results are author-reported and benchmark-specific; calibration data matters, candidate selection is manual, and the best pruning method varies by task. — FCMO-1A008E4E6967 REAP study reports strong coding retention after 50% expert pruning in two large MoE models — importance 5/10 · A May 2026 version of a Cerebras-authored preprint reports that its Router-weighted Expert Activation Pruning (REAP) method retained coding benchmark accuracy after removing 50% of experts from Qwen3-Coder-480B and Kimi-K2-Instruct. The authors summarize the non-agentic coding accuracy decreases across those two models as 0.16% at 25% compression and 1.2% at 50%; model-specific benchmark scores are reported separately in Table 3. The public repository README says router-logit normalization changed a five-model mean coding decrease from 2.6% to 1.9%, and that the large-scale results used normalized logits. These are author-reported results; no independent reproduction or serving-cost reduction is established. — FCMO-23FE07CB0846 inference_systems An open FlashAttention mapping on AMD XDNA 2 moves long-sequence attention into the compute-bound regime — importance 5/10 · A September 18 preprint compares four FlashAttention mappings on AMD XDNA 1 and XDNA 2 accelerators. On a Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 with XDNA 2, its fused MLIR-AIR mapping keeps attention-score intermediates in compute-tile memory and uses the cascade interconnect for reductions; for GPT-2 Small dimensions it reports 3.62 effective GEMM TFLOP/s at 32K sequence length, about 2.0× the IRON mapping. The authors also report 6.5× energy efficiency over an optimized Triton/ROCm integrated-GPU implementation on the same system at 32K. This is a paper-reported operator result, not end-to-end LLM serving or independently reproduced deployment performance. — FCMO-9EAC166A2708 multimodality_world_models MAAP turns cooperating robot arms into active perception viewpoints; role-conditioned control improves selected tasks — importance 5/10 · A September 18 preprint presents Multi-Agent Active Perception (MAAP), which uses wrist cameras already carried by collaborating robot arms as moving viewpoints, and Role-Aware Imitation Learning (RAIL), which predicts each arm’s manipulation or perception role and conditions its actions on that role. Across four simulated tasks, the authors report mean success rising from 56.5% with a fixed global view to 70.0% with all wrist views and 79.2% with RAIL on the same multi-view inputs. On one dual-arm real-robot placement task, the combined system succeeds in 14 of 20 trials versus 0 of 20 for fixed-view ACT, but that hardware comparison changes both visual input and controller. Results are single-training-run paper claims and do not compare against a dedicated sensing arm. — FCMO-B9E97B1EC418 reasoning_posttraining Differentiable soft-symbolic planning links visual uncertainty to rule-constrained action planning — importance 5/10 · A September 18 preprint presents a differentiable planner that keeps visual scene relations as continuous symbolic beliefs, propagates actions through soft logical transition rules, and lets the task objective update both action choices and perception parameters. On Blocksworld, the authors report 40/40 valid solutions on LatPlan-40 versus 33/40 for LatPlan and 596/600 on PlanBench-600 versus the published o1-preview score of 587/600. On a fixed 100-instance blurred-image subset, planning gradients raise valid plans from 59/100 with frozen perception to 83/100. The approach also reports results on Logistics and Sokoban. These are paper-reported, domain-specific results; solve-time and estimated-cost comparisons use different systems and are not a matched economic comparison. — FCMO-741AF584E339

The company also announced planned 2nm 800G ZR/ZR+ pluggables with MACsec and 1.6T ZR/coherent-lite demonstrations. The source establishes the company’s announcement and intended showcase, not independent observation of the demos or measured product performance. It provides no lane power, optical reach, error rate, qualification status or production schedule for the 400G/lane technology. — FCMO-A4319B48FABA efficiency Constrained binary optimization selects non-consecutive transformer blocks for depth pruning — importance 5/10 · A September 11 revision of a preprint formulates transformer-block removal as a constrained binary optimization problem. It uses second-order interactions among binary keep/remove variables, derived from calibration-set gradients, to rank block combinations; several low-energy configurations may be worth testing because the lowest-energy one is not always best downstream. Without retraining, the authors report that removing 40 of 80 Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct blocks yields 76.9 MMLU for their method versus 54.0 for block influence, a 22.9-point difference, with better scores across the listed benchmarks. Results are author-reported and benchmark-specific; calibration data matters, candidate selection is manual, and the best pruning method varies by task. — FCMO-1A008E4E6967 REAP study reports strong coding retention after 50% expert pruning in two large MoE models — importance 5/10 · A May 2026 version of a Cerebras-authored preprint reports that its Router-weighted Expert Activation Pruning (REAP) method retained coding benchmark accuracy after removing 50% of experts from Qwen3-Coder-480B and Kimi-K2-Instruct. title: Front page
summary: 1. DRYLAB-Bench reports elevated assay-based biosecurity risk scores in tool-augmented model evaluations Desk: evaluation_science Evidence: A · credible_unconfirmed · active · importance 7/10 (Very major) Importance rationale: If replicated, evidence that frontier models can prioritize measured high-risk single-substitution designs and that a tool-augmented workflow raises assay-based scores could shift biosecurity evaluation and tool-access decisions across frontier AI programs. A 7 reflects cross-team significance while the preprint, assay-bounded proxy, single-substitution scope and unresolved workflow mechanism keep the claim short of a field-reset result. What changed: A new preprint reports DRYLAB-Bench, an in-silico evaluation of biological-design outputs from 15 frontier language models across 30 policy-derived scenarios, scored against 187,695 pre-existing deep-mutational-scan measurements. The authors report that 67.6% of one-shot designs exceeded the average measured variant and 21.4% fell in the assay-specific highest-risk decile; under their tool-augmented iterative workflow, the top-decile share rose to 23.5% and the pooled Biosecurity Risk Score increased by 0.116 standard deviations. These are author-reported results from single-substitution assay proxies, not evidence of multi-variant organism-level outcomes, physical construction, or real-world harm. The paper’s sequential design does not isolate whether tool outputs or the additional deliberation cause the full increase, and no independent reproduction was inspected. Why it matters: If the reported assay-bounded results replicate, this evaluation moves biosecurity assessment beyond knowledge and refusal tests toward empirical measurement of model-generated designs and tool-augmented workflows. That could change how developers evaluate access to computational design tools. The measured single-substitution assay outcomes do not establish organism-level effects or operational threat. Demonstrated: The inspected arXiv v1 paper documents the benchmark design and reports results for 15 frontier models across 30 scenarios. Those reported measurements have not been independently reproduced in this activation. Claimed: Authors report that 67.6% of one-shot designs exceeded the average measured variant and 21.4% fell in the assay-specific top decile. In tool-augmented iterative conditions, they report a 23.5% top-decile share and a pooled Biosecurity Risk Score increase of +0.116 standard deviations. Mechanism: The authors compare model-proposed single-substitution designs in one-shot and tool-augmented iterative settings, scoring them against pre-existing deep-mutational-scan measurements. The benchmark reports assay-relative risk proxies and does not perform biological synthesis. Strongest baseline: The strongest within-paper baseline is the same model’s pre-tool one-shot submission in the same sequential trajectory. The authors also report single-round and repeated no-tool controls, but the no-tool iteration arm is under-sampled and noisy. Regime: Author-run in-silico evaluation of 15 frontier models across 30 policy-derived scenarios, with scores mapped to 187,695 pre-existing ProteinGym/ViroGym single-substitution assay measurements. It does not measure multi-variant effects, host context, transmission or physical construction. Limitations: Results are reported by the paper authors in a single preprint and were not independently reproduced in this activation.; The Biosecurity Risk Score is an assay-relative proxy based on single-substitution measurements; it does not establish multi-variant phenotypes, organism-level behavior, transmission or real-world harm.; The study’s sequential conditions do not fully separate tool-output effects from extra deliberation; the authors identify further controls that are not run.; The paper includes sensitive adversarial prompts and biological examples; this public record retains only high-level methods and aggregate results. Open evidence gaps: No independent reproduction of the benchmark scoring, model runs or aggregate risk results was inspected.; The score is bounded to single-substitution assay measurements and does not establish multi-variant effects, host-context biology, transmission, or operational real-world risk.; The within-trajectory comparison does not isolate the causal contribution of tool-output content from extra deliberation; the paper describes two unrun mechanism controls. Sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13116 2. A cryptographic construction illustrates a limit of elicitation-based model capability audits Desk: evaluation_science Evidence: A · credible_unconfirmed · active · importance 7/10 (Very major) Importance rationale: If the construction and assumptions apply to realistic model supply chains, elicitation-based audits could fail against deliberately hidden computations, motivating complementary provenance and integrity controls. The paper’s empirical demonstration is small and does not establish prevalence in deployed models. What changed: The paper constructs encrypted computations that can be embedded in model weights and conditionally hidden from polynomial-time elicitation under stated cryptographic assumptions. Its PyTorch proof of concept tests a small chemistry classifier: authors report resistance to supervised fine-tuning and latent adversarial training, while 8-bit gradient-based trigger search exhaustively enumerated 256 candidates and matched random search; the evaluated 16-bit query budget remained near chance. Correct-trigger chemistry accuracy was 73.5%. The authors verified individual compiled GLU units in Gemma 3 270M, but not the complete construction in a pretrained model. They also report raw compiled weights are anomalous, while obfuscation leaves possible within-layer correlation signals. This is a conditional construction and limited experiment, not evidence of hidden capabilities in deployed frontier models. Why it matters: The construction identifies a conditional limit for audits that rely on eliciting unwanted behavior, including white-box access, when an adversary can deliberately engineer model weights. It is a security result under cryptographic assumptions and a small proof-of-concept task, not evidence that deployed frontier models currently contain hidden dangerous capabilities. Claimed: The authors report a cryptographically locked chemistry classifier resisted supervised fine-tuning, latent adversarial training and tested trigger search under the reported settings; their 8-bit trigger search exhaustively enumerated all 256 candidates and matched random search. Mechanism: Encrypted neural networks are embedded in host weights and activated by a secret trigger; cryptographic assumptions support hardness of elicitation and interpretation even with weight access. Strongest baseline: A separately trained password-locked classifier performs the same chemistry task but has a different correct-trigger accuracy (92.7% vs 73.5%). Random-network locker control shows no observed SFT/LAT benefit. The 8-bit trigger search enumerates all candidates, so it is not evidence that gradient search beats random search. Regime: Cryptographic guarantee under the stated locker/security and compiler assumptions; empirical tests use a small 64-bit Morgan-fingerprint chemistry classifier, a 2.07-billion-parameter host construction, and three-run 95% confidence intervals for reported chemistry results. Open evidence gaps: The paper’s proof and experiments have not been independently audited or reproduced; the full construction has not been integrated into a pretrained model. Sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.13928 3. A mathematical-analysis preprint reports mismatches between OpenAI’s Navier-Stokes proof and cited Lean estimates Desk: evaluation_science Evidence: A · credible_unconfirmed · active · importance 6/10 (Major) Importance rationale: If the reported mismatches hold, a machine-checked Lean result cannot be treated as verification of the specific natural-language proof without a semantic bridge. This changes how an extraordinary mathematical claim should be evaluated, although the audit does not refute the underlying theorem. What changed: Bastounis, Circelli and Hansen compare OpenAI’s natural-language Navier–Stokes proof with cited Lean declarations. For Lemma 8.6, equation (8.19), they report that the manuscript states an m+4 derivative estimate while the cited Lean estimate requires m+5. For pressure-flux equation (10.19), they report a different Lean bound and proof route, including an additional localized gradient norm. They note one similar auxiliary bound in the repository does not appear to be directly used in the proposed theorem, leaving the effect on the actual proof dependency chain unresolved. The authors explicitly do not claim the natural-language blow-up proof is incorrect. This remains a source-reported critique in an arXiv preprint, without independent reproduction or established specialist consensus. Why it matters: A formal proof establishes its encoded theorem, but it does not by itself establish that the theorem matches the natural-language argument it is meant to check. The reported estimate differences give concrete targets for independent Lean and PDE review of an extraordinary mathematical claim, while leaving the truth of the underlying blow-up result unresolved. Claimed: The authors report an m+4 versus m+5 derivative requirement in Lemma 8.6 and a distinct pressure-flux estimate/proof route for equation (10.19), challenging correspondence between selected manuscript arguments and cited Lean declarations. Mechanism: Compares selected estimates and proof steps in OpenAI’s natural-language Navier–Stokes paper against cited Lean declarations and pinned source revisions. The critique separates encoded theorem validity from semantic fidelity to the written argument. Strongest baseline: OpenAI’s natural-language paper and its cited Lean declarations are compared directly. The authors report explicit estimate differences but do not claim the natural-language theorem is false; neither the critique nor theorem has independent peer-reviewed resolution in this review. Regime: Selected analytic estimates in one natural-language Navier-Stokes proof and corresponding Lean declarations; the paper does not audit every proof dependency or disprove the theorem. title: Research desk digest
summary: agents_memory Feedback coding reports reliable black-box covert messages in bounded LLM tests — importance 5/10 · The paper introduces Burnashev Adaptive Posterior Matching (BAM), which uses transcript feedback, posterior matching and a confirmation phase to embed messages in generated text without giving the receiver the model’s weights or prompt. On C4 RealNews, the authors report roughly 0–0.1% error for an 8-bit payload in about 46–50 tokens across three open-weight models and 1,000 trials, versus roughly 10.5–16.8% for the strongest listed black-box baseline at 50 tokens. In separate conversational experiments, error varied by model and task: Llama-3.1 and Phi-4 stayed below 3% message error, while Qwen3-A3B-30B had 19–22% dialogue error. These are one preprint’s results; no independent reproduction was found, the implementation has computational costs, and transcript editing is outside the stated security model. — FCMO-DFB3BC914F13 RoboTalk trains compact vision-language models for explicit multi-robot coordination in simulation — importance 5/10 · The revised preprint reports 7,950 FSM-validated synthetic trajectories for 53 RoboCasa-derived kitchen tasks. In closed-loop simulation, Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct reaches 65% success on 10 held-out tasks; adding rationale targets to the Thinking model reports up to 77%. These are author-reported simulator results, not physical-robot tests. — FCMO-19BFDD9D0FE6 A paper models how distractor growth can weaken evidence retrieval in long-context models — importance 5/10 · The authors formalize “context poisoning” as competition between a decisive evidence score and the maximum score among distractors. Under a softmax retrieval abstraction, they derive a finite-sample bound in which the evidence margin needed to hold accuracy above base rate grows as Ω(√log N), where N is the effective distractor count. Controlled experiments report decreasing retrieval accuracy as context grows with hard negatives; same-format distractors produce the largest drop among the tested constructions, while retrieval gating helps only when evidence recall is preserved. — FCMO-10A013EEF5C3 PhysAI-Bench reports a 52% best score on trace-derived UAV decisions — importance 5/10 · The authors present PhysAI-Bench, a multiple-choice benchmark for foundation-model action selection from trace-derived autonomous UAV missions. Its repository describes 10,178 decisions with four candidate actions, a 35-instance human-verified development set and a 500-instance episode-disjoint held-out set. After selecting a model-specific prompt and temperature configuration, the authors report GPT-5.3 Chat at 52.00% held-out decision accuracy, the highest listed score. The reference answer is the action taken in the original mission, not necessarily the only valid or globally optimal action. The repository lists the full dataset, locked split manifests, evaluation code and model outputs as release-pending. — FCMO-1F6BBDBD11C9 ActGov reports benchmark reductions in indirect prompt-injection success through per-action authorization checks — importance 5/10 · A September 2026 preprint introduces ActGov, which checks each proposed tool call against a task-scoped policy before execution. The authors report lower indirect prompt-injection success on AgentDojo and AgentDyn across four model backends, with task utility retained to varying degrees. Their cross-domain transfer test also shows severe over-restriction: an AgentDojo-trained policy has 0.100 clean-task utility on AgentDyn versus 0.767 without defense. These are paper-reported benchmark results, not independent reproduction or evidence of deployment effectiveness. — FCMO-08FB79207C91 A preprint reports that separating environmental facts from task procedures can help evolving agents — importance 5/10 · A September 21, 2026 arXiv preprint proposes TTSE, which evolves environmental facts (FACT) separately from task-conditioned procedures (TIP), using interaction evidence to revise or retire both kinds of rule. The paper frames representation errors and execution errors as distinct contributors to agent failure and evaluates the framework on ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, GDPevo, SOPBench and PinchBench. Authors report gains over selected baselines and an end-to-end PinchBench score of 0.7822 versus 0.7439 across three runs. In the SOPBench comparison, the reported dual-track gain over a single-track Bayesian-memory ablation is 2.99 percentage points over 892 tasks, but warehouse inspection contributes 78% of the gain; without that domain the reported gap is 0.67 points, and dangerous-goods tasks slightly favor single-track. In separate conversational experiments, error varied by model and task: Llama-3.1 and Phi-4 stayed below 3% message error, while Qwen3-A3B-30B had 19–22% dialogue error. Results are author-reported, unreproduced and limited to one small benchmark; the crop search also requires 16 forward passes per example. — FCMO-8CF914FD8C2A A preprint reports GPT-6 Astra leading a simulated robot benchmark, with sharp control limits — importance 5/10 · A September 21, 2026 arXiv preprint reports an evaluation of GPT-6 Astra acting directly as a robot manipulation policy, without task-specific fine-tuning or a learned motor policy in the control path. Across 42 RoboDojo simulation tasks and 2,100 trials, the authors report 22.48% average success and a score of 28.97, above the 40 public policies in their September 10 leaderboard snapshot. The result is uneven: Astra trails the top policy on precision, long-horizon and memory axes, while GPT-5.5 and DeepSeek-Flash perform much worse in the same reported interface. The authors say they stopped real-robot trials after unsafe actions damaged equipment; the paper does not establish real-world reliability or safe control. These are preprint-reported results without independent reproduction, and the public-policy runs did not receive the wiki-derived task text supplied to the LLMs. — FCMO-CA4E3C495479 INSPECT learns robot inspection views from assembly-assistant records — importance 5/10 · A September 2026 preprint introduces INSPECT, which learns robot view preferences from egocentric assembly-assistant records by separating evidence needed to resolve a claim from observation changes a robot camera can reproduce, then calibrating relative views to robot pose. In offline fixed-lattice replay on gearbox assemblies, the authors report mean human-rated view utility of 1.205 and full verifiability of 41.7% across 132 matched trials, versus 1.045 and 34.8% for the current-view baseline. On 1,068 IMPACT trials, its relative-view selector reports a 54.3% correct-decision rate versus 50.6% for current view. These are author-reported results in two constrained replay settings, not a live closed-loop deployment or independent reproduction. — FCMO-5A6AA5C74732 policy_geopolitics Et Tu, Brute? reports wealth-conditioned recommendations by personal AI agents — importance 6/10 · In a September 2026 preprint revised to v2 on September 25, authors report 325,000 experiments across 13 personal-agent configurations and three decisions: flights, health insurance and graduate programs. Eight models systematically recommend more expensive options to wealthier users under otherwise identical requests. The reported effect can persist against an explicit cheapest-option request and when wealth is inferred from task-unrelated email; the authors describe this as benchmark evidence of wealth-conditioned recommendations, not evidence of intent or field prevalence. — FCMO-2A2964A5756F UK expands AI cyber-defence pilots and begins planning for AI-agent incidents — importance 5/10 · On 12 October 2026, the UK government announced expansion of AI cyber-defence pilots and work on preparedness for serious incidents involving autonomous AI agents. It says two pilots identified and addressed more than 1,000 potential vulnerabilities, without giving a denominator, severity distribution, validation protocol or measured change in risk. A separate June case study describes weekly hackathons scanning public code across nine government organizations: it reports 407 findings in one month, £13,000 in token costs, all critical weaknesses remediated, and manual expert checks; no exploitation evidence was identified. The relationship between that case study and the October two-pilot aggregate is unspecified. The October announcement says officials will explore possible bill changes and near-miss reporting; neither is an enacted requirement. The evidence supports government program direction and an applied human-reviewed workflow, not independently measured security effectiveness. — FCMO-D148DDB68D5F Victoria sets planning and resource expectations for new data centres — importance 5/10 · Victoria’s September 2026 Sustainable Data Centre Action Plan sets out planning and resource expectations for new facilities. It describes planned planning and referral controls, expects operators to offset operational electricity use through new renewable generation and storage, and assigns project-caused connection and network augmentation costs to operators. Water measures include potable-use offsets, a water-efficiency threshold, public reporting and infrastructure cost recovery. The document reports applications seeking 19,714 megalitres annually, not approved or realized demand. Several compliance details remain under development, and the Commonwealth was developing consistent mandatory standards for a later date. — FCMO-588BC65DB51A Study reports correlated post-training hiring decisions can raise modeled systemic exclusion — importance 5/10 · A preprint studies ten base and post-trained language models in a simulated U.S. hiring workflow built from sampled occupational vacancy and career-profile distributions across 76 bachelor-level occupations. The authors report that eight of ten post-trained models became less likely to callback older applicants than their base counterparts, with a median negative shift of 4.7%. They define systemic exclusion as at least nine of ten models assigning callback probability below 0.5; under this measure, the aggregate rate rises from 5.6% for base models to 17.3% after post-training, which the authors attribute mainly to more correlated decisions. These are model outputs on generated profiles, not observed hiring decisions. The data are a snapshot of U.S. online labor markets, demographic signals are simplified, and the study does not identify which post-training stage caused the changes. — FCMO-CF1ADDC93536 Australia consults on conditions for AI training, creator rights and infrastructure investment — importance 5/10 · On September 17, 2026, Australia’s Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet opened a consultation on proposed national standards for large data centres and conditions for frontier AI training. The paper links the policy design to attracting investment while managing energy, water, community and workforce effects; it also says copyright treatment, creator protections, local research capability and compute access matter to AI training policy. The consultation asks how the government should secure local contributions and protect creators while providing regulatory certainty. It does not announce a final policy, create a copyright exception or document a company-specific bargain. Submissions closed October 9, 2026, and the paper says responses and stakeholder engagement will inform later standards. — FCMO-F0B83908B51C California signs seven data-center bills covering utility costs, reporting, water and siting — importance 5/10 · On September 21, 2026, the California Governor's Office announced the signing of seven bills addressing data-center electricity, water, reporting, environmental review and rate structures. Its summary says the package will require water and electricity reporting, place specified grid-upgrade costs on data centers, require proposed projects to provide water information to local governments and suppliers, and narrow blanket environmental exemptions. These provisions are described from the Governor's announcement; the chaptered statutes were not accessible in this review, so exact covered facilities, duties, exemptions, effective dates and implementation are not independently stated here. — FCMO-EA361C9646E9 reasoning_posttraining Critical-State RL selects trainable calls before optimizing multi-turn tool use — importance 5/10 · The preprint proposes diagnosing which occurrence in a multi-turn interaction is trainable before applying a local reinforcement-learning update. Nested sampling holds each candidate action fixed while resampling reward-only continuations to separate action-dependent signal from downstream noise. In a four-cell BFCL v4 multi_turn study using Gemma-4-26B-A4B, authors report that training the diagnostically selected recovery call raised missing-function accuracy from 0.14 to 0.283 ± 0.015 across four seeds on 200 paired examples; training the alternative decision call reduced it to 0.095. In the missing-argument category, the selected decision call rose from 0.435 to 0.473 ± 0.010, while the alternative recovery call reached 0.445. These are paper-reported results, not an independent reproduction. — FCMO-40938C5CB331 A targeted SFT and RL routing study reports gains on a bounded set of enterprise analytics skills — importance 4/10 · A preprint studies how to allocate supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL) for long-horizon analytics agents using production-mirroring beta APIs. It separates retrospectively observed trajectories into imitation, lift and discovery regimes, then uses teacher support and reward-observable headroom to route features to SFT, RL or further environment work. Across 18 subsequent feature-specific experiments, the diagnostic reportedly predicted 15 trajectories. On GPT-OSS 120B, targeted SFT-then-RL produced positive point estimates on seven of eight advertiser skills versus a frontier control; five gains had paired 95% confidence intervals excluding zero and one skill had a supported regression. A matched comparison reports a higher seven-skill mean delta with 43% less incremental RL compute than uniform routing. — FCMO-4693DEC901A7 ProcessLight applies step-level process supervision to traffic-signal control — importance 4/10 · ProcessLight/ STeP-PO trains an LLM traffic-signal controller with process-level credit: it scores intermediate traffic claims against observations, estimates each step’s effect on the final phase by removing it, and merges semantically similar steps into a tree for relative advantage assignment. The authors report Qwen2.5-3B trained on one synthetic flow and evaluated zero-shot in CityFlow on five real traffic-flow datasets from Jinan and Hangzhou; the method leads on most reported metrics. On two datasets, the paper reports lower average travel time than outcome-only RL, and a five-seed Holm-corrected analysis finds 81 of 90 baseline comparisons significant in its favor. The appendix also reports Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-32B and Llama3-8B variants and an alternate teacher, with results varying by dataset and metric. All findings remain paper-reported CityFlow simulation results for the paper’s intersection setup, not on-road deployment evidence; this review did not independently rerun the code. — FCMO-923F19836F22 Listen Then Reason weights audio test-time RL by acoustic grounding — importance 4/10 · Listen Then Reason proposes Perception-Grounded Test-Time RL (PG-TTRL) for audio-language models. It estimates each generated answer’s reliance on audio by comparing token probabilities with full audio access and with audio attention masked; a grounding margin then weights the majority-vote advantage used for unlabeled test-time RL. The authors evaluate Qwen2.5-Omni 3B and 7B on MMAR and MMAU and report higher greedy and Avg@8 scores than standard TTRL in all four model/benchmark pairings, with gains over the base model reaching 4.6 points on MMAR and 4.9 on MMAU. Majority@8 does not improve uniformly. The method adapts LoRA weights on unlabeled prompts from the benchmark test sets; added inference compute and cross-domain transfer are not established, and no independent reproduction was conducted. — FCMO-EA8DFB8BF4B2 Published edition · 2026-10-12

summary: Reviewed the six source-backed promotion-review candidates against their actual sources. Promoted five bounded developments (ActGov, LumoTree, CICL, Victoria’s data-centre action plan, and PhysAI-Bench); deferred Bonsai’s separate agentic-retention claim pending primary whitepaper access. Added paired native es-419 and zh-Hans overlays for all five new developments, stamped to the current public projection and passed locale airlock plus executor parity. Reconciled PhysAI-Bench identity to arXiv:2609.23695 and submission date 2026-09-20 after the ratchet exposed a collision; corrected the development, candidate link, archive row, and overlays before publication. Added a correction scan documenting that the earlier repository scan did not inspect the PDF. Added historical-depth summaries to the 2026-10-12 daily brief without changing the freshness assessment. Reviewed all six source-backed recent-promotion candidates against the editorial standard; reread primary sources and preserved four accepted candidates as four bounded CLAIMED/credible_unconfirmed developments, while retaining Fixed-SAE Track and Dots3-Note as deferred with specific recovery steps. Reopened the Complex KDA proof/results and THAW-VLA task/robot-cost evidence; reviewed ProcessLight method, simulation tables, appendix cross-backbone/teacher comparisons, verifier reliability, data-construction costs and author code README; reviewed Listen Then Reason test-time adaptation regime and mixed majority-vote result. Kept independent reproduction and deployment claims explicitly open. Compared the four papers’ mechanisms and compute placement: state-transition representation, cached world-model features, step-level policy credit and unlabeled test-time adaptation. The papers describe different tradeoffs between precomputation, inference and adaptation; there is no matched cost or independent comparison. Searched Chinese original-language government reporting and inspected the official State Council employment-priority plan hosted by NDRC. The plan’s AI/employment provisions are historical policy text; implementation and outcome evidence remain follow-up work. Reviewed six source-backed promotion-queue candidates against their primary sources; recorded two blocked/deferred cases, resolved one duplicate owner, and promoted three bounded paper results. Rechecked the high-impact stale Navier–Stokes, Astra and Anthropic R&D Automation records against current primary/official sources; no canonical revisions were justified. Performed partial recent-window scans across arXiv cs.AI/cs.CL/cs.LG, major lab release surfaces, official policy/regulator surfaces and a Chinese-language CAC/State Council/MIIT search; no verified material event in the approximately 36-hour window. Added four historical-depth developments with v2 importance, author-reported evidence limits, open reproduction/generalization gaps, native es-419 and zh-Hans editions, and updated the October 12 historical edition. Completed bounded recent-window sweeps of official lab/model release surfaces, arXiv cs.AI/cs.CL/cs.LG listings, and official policy/regulator surfaces; no material source event within 36 hours was identified. The arXiv pass covered only the first 50 result pages and did not advance its chronology watermark. Re-read all six queued source-backed candidates. Four were promoted with bounded paper-reported claims and explicit reproduction/attribution limits; two security claims remain deferred because the bounded claims lack accessible corroboration. Read arXiv:2610.13928v1 §§3–7, Appendix C and Appendix H. Updated FCMO-7D20901B361E with the cryptographic assumptions, experimental scope, exhaustive 8-bit trigger search, 73.5% correct-trigger result, untested 16-bit search limits, incomplete pretrained-model integration, and proposed-but-unvalidated mitigations. Authored and validated both native editions. Rechecked the highest-ranked stale Navier–Stokes development against current OpenAI formalization metadata and arXiv:2610.08144v1. The critique remains source-reported, identifies formal/natural-language mismatches, and does not assert the written theorem is false; no independent Lean build or dependency trace was performed. Refreshed the critique record access time. Targeted Chinese-language search found the Oct 10 SCIO employment briefing announcement, outside the 36-hour window. The transcript and implementing plan were not retrieved; the source check supports announcement only, not implementation or measured employment effects. Completed source-backed review of the six-item research.promotion_review_candidates queue before widening discovery: promoted SpecOpt (FCMO-168348722EE2) and RoboTalk (FCMO-19BFDD9D0FE6) as historical CLAIMED paper developments with explicit docking/simulation limits and complete es-419/zh-Hans editions; deferred CAIRN, Apple and BrowseTrace with bounded evidence gaps; linked Huawei Peerium to its existing NPO owner as duplicate. Rechecked the highest-ranked stale Navier-Stokes mathematical claim against OpenAI, its Lean repository and current Clay institutional status (SCAN-20261012T102058Z-F55A2D); updated Q-2026-10-10-NAVIER-LEAN-SEMANTIC-FIDELITY. The legacy development update was rejected by the guarded writer’s current ID/type/gap validators and was left unchanged. Performed the required approximately 36-hour primary-source sweep across arXiv, frontier-lab release surfaces and official policy/regulator sources; verified no qualifying fresh material event and recorded the partial interval and lack of watermark advancement in coverage. Reviewed all six source-backed promotion queue candidates and retained bounded deferrals or duplicate disposition with precise next steps. Updated Q-2026-09-13-NAVIER-CLEANROOM-COMPARATOR after rechecking Clay, OpenAI, arXiv and Lean project evidence; recorded conditional follow-on scope. Rechecked stale GPT-6 Astra evaluation sources; no material delta found. Promoted FCMO-6F6BB83C8EF4 from the recent arXiv announcement and inspected v1 methods, results, controls and limits; authored es-419 and zh-Hans editions. Promoted Pelican-Sim after reviewing arXiv:2609.12036v1, §§4.5–4.8 and Tables 7–14; preserved simulation-only and matched-action limits, code/reproduction gaps, and VLM evaluator dependency. Added historical edition and native translations. Promoted VideoXAgent after reviewing arXiv:2609.12818v1, abstract, §§1 and 4–5; recorded four-benchmark claims and explicitly scoped the 15% comparison to context footprint, not total token cost. Added historical edition and native translations. Reviewed four other queued candidates: unresolved primary identities for Correct-by-Construction, EmberClaw and DART; Reuters-attributed Muse report reviewed with inaccessible underlying internal posts and official page. Persisted specific next steps and debt through guarded candidate writer. Reviewed six source-backed deferred candidates against primary sources; resolved duplicates, retained one blocked issue with an exact retrieval action, and promoted bounded paper-reported results for CS-MoE, simulated hiring-bias outcomes, and MMSafe with reproduction and regime gaps preserved. Enumerated 50 recent entries each from cs.AI, cs.CL, cs.LG; assessed the Monday listing against source timestamps. The material Monday front-page story DRYLAB-Bench was reread from arXiv, but its v1 upload is 9 October and no distinct event inside the strict 36-hour window was verified. Reviewed the primary arXiv paper and author artifacts for BAM; bounded claims to the reported watermarking metrics and kept long-conversation failure, edit/delete threat limits, and exponential decoding cost explicit. Reviewed StateMem’s LIBERO, RoboMemArena and single-xArm real-robot results, contrasting task success, refresh/latency tradeoffs, baseline and embodiment scope. Reviewed DexTacWAM’s six-task real-robot table, four-task tactile-world-model ablation, action-parameterization mismatch, data/compute claims and one-platform limits. Reviewed CARE’s policy-native failure training, benchmark separation, simulation and SO-101 results; bounded its author-reported recovery gains and retained independent-reproduction and transfer gaps. Deepened the UK AI cyber announcement with its linked official case study; separated the October aggregate announcement from June pilot metrics and retained uncertainty about linkage and measured impact. Completed this Luna activation’s partial recent-window sweep across frontier-lab release surfaces, arXiv cs.AI/cs.CL/cs.LG, and official policy/regulator search. The UK government’s 12 October AI cyber-defence announcement was already represented in today’s edition and was checked against the primary release; the arXiv feed receipt from earlier today returned no Oct 11–12 submissions in its enumerated 200-item window. English-language browser queries did not establish exhaustive global coverage; the browser could not access the arXiv API in this check. Reviewed five of six queued candidates against primary sources: promoted onPanda, Embed-TTT and GAE as bounded author-reported paper developments with paired native editions; promoted DataSpace’s fixed-backbone harness spread within its 410-task benchmark scope; kept the Strands SDK claim deferred because repository existence did not substantiate its claimed comparative effect. One queued candidate, LoRA hypernetwork, remains unreviewed. For onPanda, recorded a 21-prompt, three-annotator workflow comparison and preserved interface/paradigm confounding and unaudited deployment totals. For Embed-TTT, retained the authors’ warning that embedding retrieval may reflect memorization and their interpolation-without-extrapolation limit. For DataSpace, scoped the 15.36-point spread to five tested systems with MiMo-V2.5 fixed. For GAE, scoped FVD and camera results to the two reported video datasets and kept long-horizon/world-model utility unestablished.

summary: CAND-2026-06-12-A91C37E5 — HarnessX reports large cross-benchmark gains from evolving typed agent harnesses, creating a useful contrast with HARNESSEVO's localized-credit result — revisit if: Independent reproduction appears, a paper-tagged release or exact benchmark/evolution manifests are published, or matched controls separate model/backbone, harness composition, adaptation compute, verifier leakage and component-level credit. CAND-2026-07-15-CHINA-ANTHROPOMORPHIC-AI-RULES — China's dedicated anthropomorphic-AI interaction rules enter force with dependency, manipulation and minor-protection duties — revisit if: CAC or other agencies publish enforcement cases, implementing standards, safety-assessment guidance, filing data or interpretations affecting agent memory/personalization/autonomy. CAND-2026-08-02-EU-AI-ACT-ENFORCEMENT — EU AI Act enters an enforcement phase for GPAI and transparency obligations — revisit if: Commission enforcement actions, GPAI guidance updates, Code-of-Practice implementation evidence, complaints/decisions or material court/regulator interpretations appear. CAND-2026-08-02-EU-GPAI-ENFORCEMENT — European Commission enforcement powers for general-purpose AI model obligations enter application — revisit if: The Commission announces a first GPAI enforcement action, systemic-risk notification decision, serious-incident proceeding, fine, or material interpretive update. CAND-2026-08-18-FDA-GENAI-MEDICAL-DEVICES — FDA opens competency-based regulatory framework discussion for generative-AI medical devices — revisit if: FDA publishes docket comments, workshop material, draft/final guidance, legal-authority analysis or concrete submission expectations before the deadline. CAND-2026-08-26-ANTHROPIC-CVD-SCALE — Anthropic's disclosure ledger shows AI-assisted vulnerability discovery scaling to thousands of human-reviewed findings — revisit if: The dashboard materially changes, per-model discovery attribution/cost is released, or independent organizations publish matched AI-versus-human vulnerability-discovery throughput. CAND-2026-08-26-AWS-NVIDIA-2M-GPU-EXPANSION — AWS and NVIDIA plan 2 million additional Blackwell Ultra/Rubin-class GPUs across 2027–2028 — revisit if: AWS discloses installed/deployed counts, Rubin instances reach GA, procurement/power buildout data appears, or timelines materially change. CAND-2026-08-31-3C91A8D4 — European Commission designates ChatGPT a Very Large Online Search Engine under the Digital Services Act — revisit if: The Commission publishes the designation decision, compliance deadline, systemic-risk requirements, audit/researcher-access details, enforcement actions or OpenAI implementation changes. CAND-2026-08-31-4F2C8E11 — EuroHPC signs €387.8M AMD MI430X LUMI-AI contract for 2027 deployment — revisit if: EuroHPC/CSC publish accelerator counts, peak/sustained AI performance, access policy or deployment milestones; installation begins; or the contract/system architecture materially changes. CAND-2026-08-31-54C150C8 — China MIIT launches national AI application-service-provider cultivation action — revisit if: MIIT publishes the national resource pool, procurement/compute-support figures, standards, adoption results, provider lists, or measurable model/agent deployment outcomes.
